back: Pulse — the evenly spaced beat you can tap, count, or walk to
hint: Keep it steady even when the notes change.

back: Quarter note — one beat in 4/4
hint: Say and tap one numbered beat.

back: Quarter rest — one silent beat
hint: Keep counting and move without striking.

back: Paired eighth notes — 1 &
hint: Two equal sounds inside one beat.

back: Eighth rest — silence for half of one beat
hint: Keep the pulse moving through the silent half.

back: Half note — two beats
hint: Attack once; count through the second beat.

back: Whole note — four beats in 4/4
hint: One attack lasting a full measure.

back: Meter — four steady beats fit in each measure
hint: The top number tells you how many beats to count.

back: Tie — connect the time of two notes into one held sound
hint: Do not strike again at the second note.

back: Dot — add half of the note’s own value
hint: A dotted quarter note lasts one and a half beats.

back: Offbeat — the “and” between numbered beats
hint: Count 1 & 2 & before you play it.

back: Interleaving — alternate two known ideas instead of drilling only one
hint: Switching helps you prove you can choose the right rhythm.

back: Sixteenth-note grid — four equal slots inside one beat
hint: Speak all four slots evenly.

back: Subdivision change — keep the beat steady while the number of slots changes
hint: The pulse does not speed up when the notes get smaller.

back: Snare — the large center TD-07 pad
hint: Say the mark, name, target, then relaxed center stroke.

back: Bass drum — TD-07 kick pedal and kick pad
hint: One foot press makes one bass-drum attack.

back: Closed hi-hat — left TD-07 cymbal pad
hint: Keep hi-hat pedal down; strike with a relaxed tip.

back: Crash — right TD-07 crash cymbal pad
hint: One edge strike, then let it ring.

back: Ride — right TD-07 ride cymbal pad
hint: Controlled tip stroke on the ride pad.

back: Layered groove — stacked notes happen at the same time
hint: Start with one layer, then add the next.

back: Read ahead — look at the next beat while you play the current one
hint: Keep the pulse even if you make one small error.

back: Unseen reading — scan once, count once, then keep going
hint: Do not stop to repair every mistake.

back: Keyboard landmarks — G is the treble second line; F is the bass fourth line
hint: This optional piano module is not required for the TD-07 path.

back: Interval shape — read whether notes move up, down, or stay on the same line/space pattern
hint: This is optional piano-reading support.
